Yes: [1] directly gives a probabilistic upper bound on the actor error in a slow-fast two-timescale actor-critic setup. [1] states that, with high probability, the actor parameter stays in a safe region after some finite time, and gives an explicit all-time bound on \Vert\theta_k-\theta^*\Vert for all sufficiently large k.

[3] is also about two-timescale reinforcement-learning stochastic approximation and proves stability and convergence under Markovian noise, but it does not give the same explicit probabilistic upper limit on actor distance from the optimum. [5] discusses why a two-timescale actor-critic framework helps justify second-order actor updates, but it is not an upper-bound result for actor error.
